bounded_interval_metrics.applies_to: all canonical and candidate timed runs with latency or throughput outputs

e-perf-capacity-knee.sample_unit: independent host run at one system and offered rate

ordering.method: seeded rate blocks with five-run balanced system order

e-perf-payload-refinement.sample_unit: independent host run at one payload size

e-perf-depth-extension.sample_unit: independent host run at one pipeline depth
e-perf-depth-extension.execution_path: in-process bench-source -> identical pass-through chain -> bench-sink

e-swap-independent-sessions.execution_path: in-process bench-source -> alternating pass-through-v1/v2 hot-swaps -> bench-sink

e-swap-rollback-sessions.execution_path: in-process bench-source -> process-trapping swap with automatic rollback -> bench-sink

e-compare-ekuiper-profile.sample_unit: independent host run at one rate and profiler state

ordering.method: seeded paired condition shuffle per repetition

e-val-1.purpose: Recover a known 50 ms delay before accepting downstream measurements.

e-perf-1.purpose: Compare target-load delivery and latency for the matched Pipeline A workload at 1000 messages per second; this is not a saturation-capacity measurement.

e-perf-2.purpose: Compare latency distributions for the matched Pipeline A workload at 1000 messages per second.

e-perf-3.purpose: Measure pipeline-depth scaling with MQTT bookends.

e-perf-4.purpose: Measure Wasm boundary cost across payload sizes as the paired WAFER-minus-native service-time difference.
e-perf-4.measurement_boundary: in-process path from bench-source through one pass-through transform to bench-sink; no MQTT adapter

e-perf-5.purpose: Compare WAFER/native overhead ratios across ARM64 and x86 Linux; this batch records the ARM64 half.

e-perf-6.purpose: Measure incremental RSS as Wasm pipeline depth increases.

e-perf-7.purpose: Decompose fuel and epoch metering overhead.

e-perf-8.purpose: Measure in-process latency scaling as Wasm pipeline depth increases.

e-perf-9.purpose: Compare startup after a Linux page-cache drop with subsequent warm-filesystem startup across plugin complexity tiers.
e-perf-9.warmup_exception: Startup is the measured event; warming would destroy the cold-start condition.

e-perf-10.purpose: Confirm the co-located Raspberry Pi 5 gateway-capacity envelope over the scout-derived common rate grid.

ordering.method: seeded rate blocks with thirty-run balanced system order

e-perf-10.measurement_boundary: publisher intended-offer window to subscriber receive timestamp

capacity_envelope.delivery_ceiling: bracketed by tested rates: lower bound is the highest delivery-good rate with no delivery-bad rate below it, or 0; upper bound is the lowest delivery-bad rate above every delivery-good rate, or unbounded; support-confounded rates set neither bound
capacity_envelope.competitive_decision: PASS if WAFER lower bound / eKuiper upper bound >= threshold; FAIL if WAFER upper bound / eKuiper lower bound < threshold; otherwise CENSORED

e-iso-1.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

e-iso-2.purpose: Prove cross-node memory reads are unavailable.
e-iso-2.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

e-iso-3.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

e-iso-4.purpose: Interrupt an infinite loop with epoch metering.
e-iso-4.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

infinite-loop.rationale: Fuel must not preempt the intended epoch-containment mechanism.

e-iso-5.purpose: Contain guest memory exhaustion at Store limits.
e-iso-5.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

memory-exhaust.rationale: Fuel must not preempt the intended memory-limit mechanism.

e-iso-6.purpose: Contain a guest panic without a runtime panic.
e-iso-6.warmup_exception: The first attack is observable correctness evidence and must not be excluded.

e-iso-7.purpose: Compare healthy-branch throughput and latency under parallel panic and epoch-loop faults.

epoch-loop-attack.rationale: Fuel must not preempt the intended epoch-containment mechanism.

e-iso-8.warmup_exception: Recovery begins at the first injected trap and every recovery sample is retained.

e-swap-1.purpose: Measure pause duration across repeated hot swaps.

e-swap-2.purpose: Verify zero loss and zero duplication across repeated hot swaps.

e-swap-3.purpose: Compare WAFER hot-swap, WAFER restart, and eKuiper rule restart disruption.
e-swap-3.measurement_boundary: event-aligned subscriber output around one disruption at measured t=60s

e-swap-4.purpose: Measure one stateless hot-swap centered in a true 1,000 to 2,000 to 1,000 msg/s burst per independent run.
e-swap-4.measurement_boundary: one source-driven burst and one centered swap per complete run

e-swap-5.purpose: Measure process-time failure rollback and post-rollback continuity.

e-swap-6.purpose: Decompose compile, instantiate, signal, acknowledgement, and convergence phases.

e-backpressure.purpose: Measure policy-specific saturation, accounting, and drain behavior on one bounded internal queue with a deterministic slow consumer.
e-backpressure.warmup_exception: Queue fill and drain are the measured transient; warmup would remove the event.

e-density-1.purpose: Record release Wasm component sizes beside the measured FROM scratch container floor for the isolation-unit density comparison.
e-density-1.warmup_exception: Static binary size has no runtime warmup.

verdict_rules.resampling: percentile bootstrap over runs, or over run pairs where the design pairs runs by index
verdict_rules.pilot_data: laptop shakedowns from 2026-07-21, Raspberry Pi diagnostic batches and capacity scouts

thresholds.statistic: p99 latency of each run with the injected 50 ms delay
thresholds.origin: Lower end of the tolerance for the injected 50 ms delay, introduced on 2026-07-21 together with the delay-injector plugin and its first test

thresholds.statistic: p99 latency of each run with the injected 50 ms delay
thresholds.origin: 55 ms, widened on 2026-09-02 to the upper end of the 3-significant-digit HdrHistogram bucket that holds 55 ms, when diagnostic runs already existed

thresholds.statistic: median WAFER run p95 / median eKuiper run p95 at 1,000 msg/s
thresholds.origin: RQ1 tail-latency criterion (p95 within 2x eKuiper), recorded 2026-07-04 before any eKuiper run; run-level form fixed 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: undelivered over intended messages, summed over the runs of one system
thresholds.origin: 1 percent loss limit of the rate sweep (2026-08-31), applied to the target load on 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: mean over the runs of one system of achieved / offered rate
thresholds.origin: Target-load delivery rule added on 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: duplicate deliveries summed over the runs of one system
thresholds.origin: Target-load delivery rule added on 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: median over run pairs of WAFER minus native service-time p50 at one payload size
thresholds.origin: RQ1 per-hop reference (under 50 microseconds per boundary crossing), recorded 2026-07-04 before any payload run; paired WAFER-minus-native form adopted 2026-10-01

thresholds.statistic: pooled loss of one system at one tested rate
thresholds.origin: 1 percent loss limit of the rate sweep, introduced 2026-08-31

thresholds.statistic: mean achieved / offered ratio of one system at one tested rate
thresholds.origin: Added with the trace-free capacity envelope on 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: duplicate deliveries of one system at one tested rate
thresholds.origin: Added with the trace-free capacity envelope on 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: WAFER / eKuiper tested-grid delivery ceiling, as the interval between the two brackets
thresholds.origin: RQ1 competitiveness criterion (within 30 percent of eKuiper), recorded 2026-07-04 before any eKuiper run; bracketed ratio form fixed 2026-09-04 and 2026-10-01

thresholds.statistic: runs of one attack that its expected mechanism did not contain, counting runs the runtime did not survive
thresholds.origin: RQ2: every attack scenario contained, recorded 2026-07-04 before the first containment run

thresholds.statistic: drop of the median branch-A run throughput below the control median, in percent of the control median
thresholds.origin: RQ2 healthy-branch criterion (under 1 percent throughput impact), recorded 2026-07-04 before the first E-Iso-7 run

thresholds.statistic: attack runs the runtime did not survive
thresholds.origin: Runs the system under test ended counted as failures since 2026-10-01

thresholds.statistic: E-Swap-1 runs with loss, duplicates or an early stop
thresholds.origin: RQ3 message accounting (zero loss, zero duplication), recorded by 2026-07-12, before any E-Swap run

thresholds.statistic: median over WAFER hot-swap runs of the event-aligned throughput dip
thresholds.origin: RQ3 throughput-dip criterion (under 5 percent), recorded 2026-07-04 before any E-Swap-3 run; upper-bound form fixed 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: WAFER hot-swap runs with loss, duplicates or an early stop
thresholds.origin: RQ3 message accounting (zero loss, zero duplication), recorded by 2026-07-12, before any E-Swap run

thresholds.statistic: nearest-rank p95 over runs of the sink-observed gap, one swap per run
thresholds.origin: 100 ms swap pause target of the first specification (2026-02-14), written before the runtime existed; across-run sink-gap form fixed 2026-09-04

thresholds.statistic: runs with full-run loss, duplicates or an early stop
thresholds.origin: RQ3 message accounting (zero loss, zero duplication), recorded by 2026-07-12, before any E-Swap run

thresholds.statistic: runs with a failed rollback, no output after the final rollback, loss or duplicates
thresholds.origin: RQ3 failed-replacement recovery (the pipeline survives and loses no message), recorded by 2026-07-19, before any E-Swap run

replication_concordance.direction: the side of the declared threshold on which a host's point estimate falls, the count itself for an exact count: it meets the threshold or misses it

classes.rule: either host lacks the criterion, reports it PENDING or has no point estimate
both hosts report the same PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE verdict
the verdicts differ and both point estimates fall on the same side of the threshold
the verdicts differ and the point estimates fall on opposite sides of the threshold

replication_concordance.precedence: the first class in the listed order whose rule holds
replication_concordance.canonical_verdict: unchanged: replication reports agreement with the canonical host and never alters its verdict
